title: Architecture Standards: Unified Guidelines and ADRs (consolidated)
author: Sana Patel
body:
Overview:

This consolidated guidance describes Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also catalogs Decision Records (ADRs) adopted by the platform teams and prescribes the review and rollout process for future changes. The goal is to provide a single, actionable reference for engineers designing and operating production inference services.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted Redwood API, Dedicated, and Private deployment workstreams.
- Includes public API surface, backend service contracts, infra provisioning, model-serving runtime, telemetry, and SLO targets.
- Excludes customer-specific security controls documented under security-and-compliance.

Principles (high level):
1) Backwards compatibility: public API changes MUST follow the API versioning policy (see API Standards).
2) Observable by default: services must emit traces, metrics, and structured logs for every request path.
3) Safe rollout: every change touching runtime, routing, or model-serving must include a canary + automated rollback plan.
4) Cost-aware design: choices should include estimated per-token cost and latency impact.

1. API Standards
- Purpose: Ensure consistent, predictable developer experience across endpoints (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking).
- Versioning: Use path-based major versions: /v1/, /v2/. Minor changes are additive and non-breaking; breaking changes require a new major.
- Contract style: JSON over HTTPS. Request/response schemas are defined in OpenAPI 3.1 and stored in the api-specs repo.
- Error model: Use HTTP status semantics plus structured error payload: {"code": string, "message": string, "details": opt-object}. Retryable errors set retryable=true in details.
- Pagination & streaming: Streaming uses server-sent events (SSE) for tokens. Paginated endpoints follow cursor patterns with page_size and next_cursor.
- Authentication: Bearer tokens (short-lived) + optional mTLS for Dedicated and Private control planes. Keys are rotated per the security policy.
- API review checklist: swagger spec, backward-compatibility matrix, performance estimate, telemetry hooks, and test vectors.

API Example (excerpt - generation):
POST /v1/generate
Request JSON:
{
  "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
  "input": "Summarize the following text...",
  "max_tokens": 512
}
Response JSON (streaming uses SSE events with "token" payload):
{
  "id": "req_123",
  "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
  "output": "..."
}

2. Coding Standards
- Language conventions: follow the canonical style guides per repository (Go: effective_go + gofmt; Python: PEP8 + black; TypeScript: Airbnb + Prettier).
- Module ownership: each service repo must have an OWNER file listing maintainers and an oncall rotation.
- Testing: unit tests >= 80% critical path coverage for core runtime services; integration tests must run in CI using small fixture clusters.
- Static analysis: enable linting, type-checking (mypy/tsc), and dependence scanning in CI.
- Code review: all changes require 2 approvals for non-security repos; security-sensitive changes require security-approved checklist.
- Secrets: never commit secrets. Use secrets manager integrations and local tooling (redwood-secrets-cli) for dev testing.

3. Infrastructure Standards
- IaC: Terraform modules are the canonical source for cloud resources. Modules must be versioned and published to the internal module registry.
- Environment parity: dev/staging/prod must share the same module configurations with environment-specific parameters only.
- Networking: default deny security groups; private subnets for inference GPUs; NATs for control-plane egress.
- Capacity: GPU fleet autoscaling governed by the capacity-planning playbook; Reserved capacity pools for Dedicated are declared in capacity manifests.
- CI/CD: Blue/green or canary deployments for services exposing customer-facing endpoints. Infrastructure changes require plan & apply in CI with manual approval for prod.

Recommended Terraform module table:
| Module | Purpose | Required vars | Owner | Notes |
|--------|---------|---------------|-------|-------|
| redwood/gke-cluster | K8s control plane | project, region, node_pools | eng-infra | Use standard node taints for runtime |
| redwood/gpu-fleet | GPU provisioning | instance_type, accelerator_count | eng-infra | Integrate with capacity planner |

4. Model-Serving Standards
- Model packaging: models must ship as versioned artifacts with manifest.yaml including architecture, tokenizer, model_size, quantization_profiles.
- Runtime compatibility: models must declare runtime compatibility matrix (e.g., runtime v2.1, kernels: triton/torchscript/fuser).
- Quantization: approved profiles stored under quantization-profiles with measured perf/quality tradeoffs. Changes to profiles require an ADR if they alter default behavior.
- KV cache and prefix caching: services must expose cache metrics (hit_rate, miss_rate, avg_latency) and include cache-busting semantics for model updates.
- Rollouts: model rollouts use staged canaries (1%, 10%, 50%) with quality evaluation hooks. Canary success criteria: no regression on chosen eval suites, latency within 10% of baseline, error rates below SLO thresholds.

Model manifest example:
---
name: redwood-alpha-1
version: 2026-04-15
architecture: transformer
vocab: sentencepiece-v1
quantization_profiles: [q8_0.9, q4_0.7]
compatibility: [runtime>=2.0, kernel=fused_attention]
---

5. Observability Standards
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans for request lifecycle. Traces MUST include model_id, request_id, tenant_id, route, and tokens_processed.
- Metrics: Prometheus metric conventions (snake_case, unit suffix). Core metrics: request_latency_ms, tokens_generated_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio, model_load_time_seconds, inference_errors_total.
- Logs: Structured JSON logs with severity, timestamp, request_id, span_id. PII must be redacted before emission.
- Dashboards & Alerts: Per-model and per-route dashboards. Alerts: P99 latency > SLO for 15m, error_rate > 0.5% 5m, model_load_time > 30s. Escalation playbooks live in eng-sre/runbooks.

Telemetry tagging convention sample:
- service.name: string
- service.version: semver
- model.id: string
- deployment.environment: prod | staging | dev

6. Performance Standards and SLOs
- Latency SLOs (hosted API): P50 < 50ms for small models (<= 2B tokens), P95 < 200ms general target for text generation endpoints; per-route SLOs documented in route config.
- Throughput: per-GPU throughput baselines documented in benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Batching and prefix caching are first-order levers to meet throughput targets.
- Cost targets: include per-token amortized GPU compute estimate in PRs that change model size or serving config.
- Performance testing: every release to runtime must run the perf-suite with standard workloads and publish results to the perf dashboard.

7. Decision Records (ADRs) - summary of key decisions
- ADR-2025-01: API versioning strategy (path-based major versions) — adopted 2025-06-01.
- ADR-2025-08: Default telemetry (OpenTelemetry) — adopted 2025-09-12.
- ADR-2026-02: Quantization profile naming and compatibility policy — adopted 2026-02-20.
- ADR-2026-07: Fallback routing policy for capacity shortages (tiered model variants) — adopted 2026-07-15.
- ADR-2026-11: Model manifest schema v2 (adds compatibility field and perf metadata) — adopted 2026-11-30.

Each ADR entry includes: title, date, status, motivation, alternatives considered, decision, and consequences. Full ADRs reside in the decision-records folder and are referenced from related_pages.

8. Ownership & Responsibilities
- Architecture steward: Marcus Lee (eng-platform) — maintains this consolidated doc and chairs quarterly standards review.
- API standards owner: Arielle Kim (eng-developer-experience).
- Runtime and model-serving owner: Diego Ramirez (eng-serving-runtime).
- Observability owner: Eng SRE team (see eng-sre/runbooks).

9. Change and Rollout Process
1. Proposal: Open a design doc and PR against api-specs or infra modules. Include compatibility matrix, perf estimate, telemetry changes, and rollback plan.
2. Review: Obtain reviewers listed in the metadata and SOC/security review if applicable.
3. Staging test: Deploy canary to staging and run perf + eval suites.
4. Canary: Stage canary sizes per model-serving standards and monitor SLOs for a minimum of 1 hour under production-like load.
5. Gradual rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated checks and rollback triggers.
6. Post-mortem: Document any incidents in oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems and update standards if required.

Appendix: Example rollout checklist (required for model/runtime changes)
- [ ] ADR lookup: confirm no conflicting ADRs.
- [ ] Spec PR: OpenAPI + schema changes.
- [ ] Perf estimate: quantified cost/latency delta.
- [ ] Canary plan: traffic allocation and monitoring queries.
- [ ] Eval set: reference prompts and regression thresholds.
- [ ] Alert thresholds: updated and routed to eng-sre.
- [ ] Rollback steps: documented and tested.

Appendix: Configuration table (example defaults)
| Config | Default | Notes |
| model_canary_steps | [1,10,50] | percentage rollout steps |
| default_latency_slo_p95_ms | 200 | general generation SLO |
| cache_ttl_seconds | 300 | prefix/KV cache default TTL |

Contact and feedback:
Send comments or proposed changes via pull request to the architecture standards repo and notify @marcus-lee. Quarterly standards review meetings are scheduled; see eng-platform/roadmap for dates.
